user: my brother is in the hospital with cancer and im trying to study for my databases exam but i cant focus, can you explain left join vs inner join in a way that might actually stick
reply:
I'm really sorry about your brother. That's a lot to carry while you're trying to study, and it makes sense that focus is hard right now.

Here's a way to remember the difference: an inner join is the overlap of two circles, so it only keeps rows that match on both sides. A left join keeps everything on the left, and fills in blanks on the right where nothing matches. If you're asking "which students have enrolled in a class," an inner join drops students with no classes. A left join keeps them and shows empty class fields.

If it helps, tell me what your exam covers and we can go through a practice query together, one small step at a time.
